---- MODULE W4Od9m0p2t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Controllers, Blocks, Feeders, MaxVersion, Unallocated, NoStage

\* A staging records the table version it was read against; it deliberately does
\* not move the block, which is why a controller dying mid-decision is harmless.
Stagings == [block : Blocks, feeder : Feeders, base : 0..MaxVersion]

VARIABLES committed, allocation, escrow, version, staged, dead

vars == <<committed, allocation, escrow, version, staged, dead>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ committed \in SUBSET Blocks
    /\ allocation \in [Blocks -> {Unallocated} \cup Feeders]
    /\ escrow \in SUBSET Blocks
    /\ version \in 0..MaxVersion
    /\ staged \in [Controllers -> {NoStage} \cup Stagings]
    /\ dead \in SUBSET Controllers

Init ==
    /\ committed = {}
    /\ allocation = [b \in Blocks |-> Unallocated]
    /\ escrow = {}
    /\ version = 0
    /\ staged = [c \in Controllers |-> NoStage]
    /\ dead = {}

CommitBlock(b) ==
    /\ b \notin committed
    /\ committed' = committed \cup {b}
    /\ escrow' = escrow \cup {b}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<allocation, version, staged, dead>>

Stage(c, b, f) ==
    /\ c \notin dead
    /\ staged[c] = NoStage
    /\ b \in escrow
    /\ staged' = [staged EXCEPT ![c] = [block |-> b, feeder |-> f, base |-> version]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<committed, allocation, escrow, version, dead>>

Usable(c) ==
    /\ c \notin dead
    /\ staged[c].base = version
    /\ staged[c].block \in escrow
    /\ version < MaxVersion

\* The block leaves escrow and lands on the feeder in the same step, so the
\* accounting never has it in both places or in neither.
Apply(c) ==
    /\ staged[c] # NoStage
    /\ Usable(c)
    /\ allocation' = [allocation EXCEPT ![staged[c].block] = staged[c].feeder]
    /\ escrow' = escrow \ {staged[c].block}
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ staged' = [staged EXCEPT ![c] = NoStage]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<committed, dead>>

StartOver(c) ==
    /\ staged[c] # NoStage
    /\ ~Usable(c)
    /\ staged' = [staged EXCEPT ![c] = NoStage]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<committed, allocation, escrow, version, dead>>

Fail(c) ==
    /\ c \notin dead
    /\ Cardinality(dead) < Cardinality(Controllers)
    /\ dead' = dead \cup {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<committed, allocation, escrow, version, staged>>

Revive(c) ==
    /\ c \in dead
    /\ dead' = dead \ {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<committed, allocation, escrow, version, staged>>

Release(b) ==
    /\ allocation[b] # Unallocated
    /\ allocation' = [allocation EXCEPT ![b] = Unallocated]
    /\ escrow' = escrow \cup {b}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<committed, version, staged, dead>>

Decommit(b) ==
    /\ b \in escrow
    /\ committed' = committed \ {b}
    /\ escrow' = escrow \ {b}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<allocation, version, staged, dead>>

Reindex ==
    /\ version = MaxVersion
    /\ version' = 0
    /\ staged' = [c \in Controllers |-> NoStage]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<committed, allocation, escrow, dead>>

Settle(c) == Apply(c) \/ StartOver(c)

Next ==
    \/ \E b \in Blocks : CommitBlock(b) \/ Release(b) \/ Decommit(b)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers, b \in Blocks, f \in Feeders : Stage(c, b, f)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Settle(c) \/ Fail(c) \/ Revive(c)
    \/ Reindex

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
        /\ \A c \in Controllers : WF_vars(Settle(c))

BlocksAccountedFor ==
    committed = escrow \cup {b \in Blocks : allocation[b] # Unallocated}

EveryStagingClears ==
    \A c \in Controllers : (staged[c] # NoStage) ~> (staged[c] = NoStage)

====
nl:
A power-grid load shedder allocates fixed megawatt blocks to feeders. A block that a
generator has committed is accounted for in exactly one of two ways: it is either held in the
shedder's escrow, waiting to be allocated, or it is allocated to a feeder. Nothing else may
ever be true of a committed block -- a block that fell out of escrow without landing on a
feeder would be power the grid thinks it has and does not.

Allocations are made under optimistic locking. A controller stages the block and feeder it
intends to pair, together with the allocation table's version as it read it, and the staged
pairing is applied only if that version is still the table's version, the block is still in
escrow, and the version numbering has room. Otherwise the staging is thrown away and the
controller starts over.

A controller can fail silently, and it can fail with a staging outstanding. That is safe
precisely because a staging does not move the block: the block sits in escrow until an
application actually lands, so a controller that dies mid-decision costs the grid nothing but
the staging, which is later thrown away like any other unusable one. A failed controller may
come back.

The shedder behaves as follows. A generator may commit a block that is not yet committed,
which puts it into escrow. A live controller with nothing staged may stage a block that is in
escrow against a feeder, recording the table's version. A live controller may apply its
staging when the version still matches, the block is still in escrow, and the numbering has
room, which takes the block out of escrow, allocates it to the feeder and moves the version
on. A staging that fails any of those tests, or whose controller has failed, is thrown away.
A controller may fail silently, so long as not all of them have. A failed controller may come
back. An allocated block may be released back into escrow. A block sitting in escrow may be
decommitted, which withdraws it from the grid's committed set entirely. When the version
numbering is spent it is reindexed, which also throws away every staging.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The committed blocks are exactly those held in escrow together with those
allocated to feeders, so no committed block is ever conjured up or mislaid.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every staging a controller makes is eventually cleared.

---- MODULE W4Od1m3p3t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Towers, Slots, Flights, MaxTerm, NoFlight

VARIABLES onSlot, confirmed, believes, term, dead

vars == <<onSlot, confirmed, believes, term, dead>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ onSlot \in [Slots -> {NoFlight} \cup Flights]
    /\ confirmed \in SUBSET Flights
    /\ believes \in [Towers -> 0..MaxTerm]
    /\ term \in 1..MaxTerm
    /\ dead \in SUBSET Towers

Init ==
    /\ onSlot = [s \in Slots |-> NoFlight]
    /\ confirmed = {}
    /\ believes = [t \in Towers |-> 1]
    /\ term = 1
    /\ dead = {}

\* Only the tower whose believed term is the live one may hand out a slot; a
\* tower demoted while it was merely quiet finds its belief worthless.
Leading(t) == t \notin dead /\ believes[t] = term

Allocate(t, f, s) ==
    /\ Leading(t)
    /\ onSlot[s] = NoFlight
    /\ f \notin confirmed
    /\ onSlot' = [onSlot EXCEPT ![s] = f]
    /\ confirmed' = confirmed \cup {f}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<believes, term, dead>>

Cancel(s) ==
    /\ onSlot[s] # NoFlight
    /\ confirmed' = confirmed \ {onSlot[s]}
    /\ onSlot' = [onSlot EXCEPT ![s] = NoFlight]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<believes, term, dead>>

Fail(t) ==
    /\ t \notin dead
    /\ Cardinality(dead) < Cardinality(Towers)
    /\ dead' = dead \cup {t}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<onSlot, confirmed, believes, term>>

\* A tower comes back believing exactly what it believed when it went down.
Restore(t) ==
    /\ t \in dead
    /\ dead' = dead \ {t}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<onSlot, confirmed, believes, term>>

TakeOver(t) ==
    /\ t \notin dead
    /\ believes[t] # term
    /\ term < MaxTerm
    /\ term' = term + 1
    /\ believes' = [believes EXCEPT ![t] = term + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<onSlot, confirmed, dead>>

Renumber(t) ==
    /\ term = MaxTerm
    /\ Leading(t)
    /\ term' = 1
    /\ believes' = [x \in Towers |-> IF x = t THEN 1 ELSE 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<onSlot, confirmed, dead>>

Next ==
    \/ \E t \in Towers, f \in Flights, s \in Slots : Allocate(t, f, s)
    \/ \E s \in Slots : Cancel(s)
    \/ \E t \in Towers : Fail(t) \/ Restore(t) \/ TakeOver(t) \/ Renumber(t)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

SlotRecordsAgree ==
    confirmed = {onSlot[s] : s \in Slots} \ {NoFlight}

====
nl:
An air-traffic runway allocator hands departure slots to flights. It keeps two records that
must always agree: a per-slot record of the flight occupying it, and the set of flights the
allocator has confirmed a slot to. A slot handed out twice would evict the flight that had it,
leaving that flight confirmed with no slot to stand on, which is exactly the disagreement
between the two records that must never arise.

Allocation is done by whichever tower is currently leading, and leadership is carried by a
term number: a tower may allocate only while the term it believes it holds is the allocator's
current term. A tower can fail silently, so the others cannot tell a failed tower from a quiet
one and any tower may take over, which raises the term and leaves the previous leader believing
a term that no longer counts. A failed tower may come back, still believing whatever term it
believed when it went down.

The allocator behaves as follows. A live tower whose believed term is the current term may
allocate a free slot to a flight that has no slot confirmed, which records the flight against
the slot and confirms the slot to the flight. A slot's allocation may be cancelled, which
clears the slot and withdraws the confirmation together. Any tower may fail silently, so long
as not every tower has failed, and a failed tower may come back. A live tower whose believed
term is not the current term may take over, raising the term and taking it for itself, so long
as the term numbering has room. When the numbering is spent, a live tower believing the
current term may restart the numbering with itself leading and every other tower believing
nothing.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The set of flights confirmed a slot is exactly the set of flights appearing
in the per-slot record, so no slot is ever handed out a second time behind the first flight's
back.

---- MODULE W4Od4m3p3t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Controllers, Bays, Vehicles, MaxTerm, NoVehicle, NoBay, NoClaim

Claims == [veh : Vehicles, bay : Bays]

VARIABLES inBay, gotBay, claim, leader, term

vars == <<inBay, gotBay, claim, leader, term>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ inBay \in [Bays -> {NoVehicle} \cup Vehicles]
    /\ gotBay \in [Vehicles -> {NoBay} \cup Bays]
    /\ claim \in [Controllers -> {NoClaim} \cup Claims]
    /\ leader \in Controllers
    /\ term \in 1..MaxTerm

Init ==
    /\ inBay = [b \in Bays |-> NoVehicle]
    /\ gotBay = [v \in Vehicles |-> NoBay]
    /\ claim = [c \in Controllers |-> NoClaim]
    /\ leader \in Controllers
    /\ term = 1

Post(c, v, b) ==
    /\ c = leader
    /\ claim[c] = NoClaim
    /\ inBay[b] = NoVehicle
    /\ gotBay[v] = NoBay
    /\ claim' = [claim EXCEPT ![c] = [veh |-> v, bay |-> b]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inBay, gotBay, leader, term>>

\* The acknowledgement re-tests what the claim assumed; a claim posted by a
\* controller that has since been replaced fails here rather than being recalled.
Standing(c) ==
    /\ inBay[claim[c].bay] = NoVehicle
    /\ gotBay[claim[c].veh] = NoBay

Acknowledge(c) ==
    /\ claim[c] # NoClaim
    /\ Standing(c)
    /\ inBay' = [inBay EXCEPT ![claim[c].bay] = claim[c].veh]
    /\ gotBay' = [gotBay EXCEPT ![claim[c].veh] = claim[c].bay]
    /\ claim' = [claim EXCEPT ![c] = NoClaim]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term>>

Withdraw(c) ==
    /\ claim[c] # NoClaim
    /\ ~Standing(c)
    /\ claim' = [claim EXCEPT ![c] = NoClaim]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inBay, gotBay, leader, term>>

Empty(b) ==
    /\ inBay[b] # NoVehicle
    /\ gotBay' = [gotBay EXCEPT ![inBay[b]] = NoBay]
    /\ inBay' = [inBay EXCEPT ![b] = NoVehicle]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<claim, leader, term>>

TakeCharge(c) ==
    /\ c # leader
    /\ term < MaxTerm
    /\ leader' = c
    /\ term' = term + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inBay, gotBay, claim>>

Restart ==
    /\ term = MaxTerm
    /\ term' = 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inBay, gotBay, claim, leader>>

Resolve(c) == Acknowledge(c) \/ Withdraw(c)

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Controllers, v \in Vehicles, b \in Bays : Post(c, v, b)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Resolve(c)
    \/ \E b \in Bays : Empty(b)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : TakeCharge(c)
    \/ Restart

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
        /\ \A c \in Controllers : WF_vars(Resolve(c))

BaysMirrorVehicles ==
    \A v \in Vehicles : gotBay[v] # NoBay => inBay[gotBay[v]] = v

EveryClaimResolves ==
    \A c \in Controllers : (claim[c] # NoClaim) ~> (claim[c] = NoClaim)

====

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Controllers = {ctrlLine, ctrlRelief}
    Bays = {bayFoam, bayDry}
    Vehicles = {vehSedan, vehVan}
    MaxTerm = 2
    NoVehicle = noVehicle
    NoBay = noBay
    NoClaim = noClaim

INVARIANT BaysMirrorVehicles
PROPERTY EveryClaimResolves
nl:
A car-wash conveyor line assigns arriving vehicles to wash bays. It keeps a per-bay record of
the vehicle in it and a per-vehicle record of the bay it was given, and these must be exact
mirrors of one another: a bay given out twice would leave the first vehicle still pointing at
a bay that now holds someone else.

Assignment is a two-step handshake. The controller in charge posts a claim naming a vehicle
and a bay; the claim is only turned into an assignment when the line acknowledges it, and only
if the bay is still empty and the vehicle still has no bay. Controllers can be slow but never
fail, so a posted claim may sit unacknowledged for arbitrarily long, yet it is always resolved
in the end, one way or the other.

Because a controller can be slow, the line may elect a different controller while a claim of
the old one is still outstanding, which raises the term. The stale controller's claim is not
recalled; it simply has to fail the acknowledgement test if the bay it named has been taken in
the meantime, and is withdrawn instead.

The line behaves as follows. The controller whose term is the line's current term may post a
claim naming an empty bay and a vehicle with no bay, if it has no claim outstanding. An
outstanding claim whose bay is still empty and whose vehicle still has no bay may be
acknowledged, which writes both records and clears the claim. An outstanding claim that fails
either test is withdrawn. An occupied bay may be emptied, which clears both records together.
Any controller other than the one in charge may take over, which raises the term, so long as
the term numbering has room. When the numbering is spent, the controller in charge may restart
it.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every vehicle that has been given a bay is the vehicle that bay records
holding, so no bay is ever handed out a second time.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every claim a controller posts is eventually resolved, leaving that
controller with no claim outstanding.

---- MODULE W4Od8m7p1t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Departments, Revisions, NoRev

VARIABLES head, parent, published, drafting, dead

vars == <<head, parent, published, drafting, dead>>

\* Walking back from the head along parent links, with fuel so the walk is
\* guaranteed to terminate however the links happen to be arranged.
RECURSIVE Reaches(_, _, _)
Reaches(r, h, fuel) ==
    IF h = NoRev \/ fuel = 0 THEN FALSE
    ELSE IF h = r THEN TRUE
    ELSE Reaches(r, parent[h], fuel - 1)

OnChain(r) == Reaches(r, head, Cardinality(Revisions) + 1)

TypeOK ==
    /\ head \in {NoRev} \cup Revisions
    /\ parent \in [Revisions -> {NoRev} \cup Revisions]
    /\ published \in SUBSET Revisions
    /\ drafting \in [Departments -> {NoRev} \cup Revisions]
    /\ dead \in SUBSET Departments

Init ==
    /\ head = NoRev
    /\ parent = [r \in Revisions |-> NoRev]
    /\ published = {}
    /\ drafting = [d \in Departments |-> NoRev]
    /\ dead = {}

Unused(r) ==
    /\ parent[r] = NoRev
    /\ r \notin published
    /\ r # head
    /\ \A e \in Departments : drafting[e] # r

StartDraft(d, r) ==
    /\ d \notin dead
    /\ drafting[d] = NoRev
    /\ Unused(r)
    /\ drafting' = [drafting EXCEPT ![d] = r]
    /\ parent' = [parent EXCEPT ![r] = head]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<head, published, dead>>

\* The swap only lands while the head is still what the draft was parented on.
Publish(d) ==
    /\ d \notin dead
    /\ drafting[d] # NoRev
    /\ parent[drafting[d]] = head
    /\ head' = drafting[d]
    /\ published' = published \cup {drafting[d]}
    /\ drafting' = [drafting EXCEPT ![d] = NoRev]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<parent, dead>>

Abandon(d) ==
    /\ drafting[d] # NoRev
    /\ parent[drafting[d]] # head
    /\ parent' = [parent EXCEPT ![drafting[d]] = NoRev]
    /\ drafting' = [drafting EXCEPT ![d] = NoRev]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<head, published, dead>>

Fail(d) ==
    /\ d \notin dead
    /\ Cardinality(dead) < Cardinality(Departments)
    /\ dead' = dead \cup {d}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<head, parent, published, drafting>>

Revive(d) ==
    /\ d \in dead
    /\ dead' = dead \ {d}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<head, parent, published, drafting>>

Next ==
    \/ \E d \in Departments, r \in Revisions : StartDraft(d, r)
    \/ \E d \in Departments : Publish(d) \/ Abandon(d) \/ Fail(d) \/ Revive(d)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

PublishedStaysOnChain == \A r \in Revisions : r \in published => OnChain(r)

====
nl:
A university course-registration system keeps its course catalogue as a chain of revisions. A
single compare-and-swap register holds the head of the chain. A department that wants to change
the catalogue starts a draft revision, recording as the draft's parent whatever the head was at
the moment the draft began. Publishing swaps the head to the draft, but only if the head is
still the revision the draft was parented on; otherwise the draft is stale, because publishing
it would hang the chain off an old head and cut loose everything published in between, and the
department has to abandon it and start again.

A department can fail silently, so the others cannot tell a failed department from a slow one.
A department that fails with a draft outstanding costs the catalogue nothing: the draft was
never on the chain, so abandoning it later loses no published work. A failed department may
come back.

The system behaves as follows. A live department with no draft outstanding may start a draft on
a revision number that is unused -- not parented on anything, not published, not the head, and
not being drafted elsewhere -- recording the current head as that revision's parent. A live
department may publish its draft when the head is still the revision the draft is parented on,
which makes the draft the new head and records it as published. A department may abandon a
draft whose parent is no longer the head, clearing the revision number for reuse. A department
may fail silently, so long as not every department has failed, and a failed department may come
back.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every revision that has been published still lies on the chain of parents
running back from the current head, so no published revision is ever cut loose by a later
publish.

---- MODULE W4Od19m4p4t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Requests, Capacity, QueueLimit

VARIABLES free, inTransit, onShelf, queue

vars == <<free, inTransit, onShelf, queue>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ free \in 0..Capacity
    /\ inTransit \in 0..Capacity
    /\ onShelf \in 0..Capacity
    /\ queue \in SUBSET Requests

Init ==
    /\ free = Capacity
    /\ inTransit = 0
    /\ onShelf = 0
    /\ queue = {}

\* Backpressure: the queue simply will not grow past its limit.
Join(r) ==
    /\ r \notin queue
    /\ Cardinality(queue) < QueueLimit
    /\ queue' = queue \cup {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<free, inTransit, onShelf>>

\* Dispatching moves a permit from the free pool onto an instruction; the permit
\* is spoken for from that moment, not from when the instruction lands.
Dispatch(r) ==
    /\ r \in queue
    /\ free > 0
    /\ free' = free - 1
    /\ inTransit' = inTransit + 1
    /\ queue' = queue \ {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED onShelf

Defer(r) ==
    /\ r \in queue
    /\ free = 0
    /\ queue' = queue \ {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<free, inTransit, onShelf>>

\* Instructions land in whatever order they get to; which one lands is not fixed
\* by which was sent first.
Land ==
    /\ inTransit > 0
    /\ inTransit' = inTransit - 1
    /\ onShelf' = onShelf + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<free, queue>>

Recall ==
    /\ inTransit > 0
    /\ inTransit' = inTransit - 1
    /\ free' = free + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<onShelf, queue>>

Collect ==
    /\ onShelf > 0
    /\ onShelf' = onShelf - 1
    /\ free' = free + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inTransit, queue>>

Clear(r) == Dispatch(r) \/ Defer(r)

Next ==
    \/ \E r \in Requests : Join(r) \/ Clear(r)
    \/ Land
    \/ Recall
    \/ Collect

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
        /\ \A r \in Requests : WF_vars(Clear(r))

PermitsAccountForCapacity == free + inTransit + onShelf = Capacity

EveryQueuedRequestLeaves ==
    \A r \in Requests : (r \in queue) ~> (r \notin queue)

====

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Requests = {reqAtlas, reqOdes, reqManual, reqChart}
    Capacity = 3
    QueueLimit = 2

INVARIANT PermitsAccountForCapacity
PROPERTY EveryQueuedRequestLeaves
nl:
A library reservation system runs a hold shelf with a fixed number of shelf permits. A permit
is what entitles a book to occupy space: the shelf's whole capacity is accounted for at every
moment as permits still free, permits travelling with a placement instruction that has not
landed yet, and permits under books already on the shelf.

Pickup requests wait in a bounded work queue. The queue applies backpressure by refusing to
grow beyond its limit. Dispatching a request takes a free permit and sends a placement
instruction; instructions do not land in the order they were sent, so several may be
outstanding at once and any of them may be the next to land. An instruction may also be
recalled in transit, which hands its permit straight back.

The system behaves as follows. A pickup request may join the queue while the queue is below
its limit. A queued request may be dispatched while a permit is free, which takes that permit
and puts a placement instruction in transit. A queued request is deferred off the queue
instead when no permit is free. A placement instruction in transit may land, putting a book on
the shelf under the permit it was carrying. A placement instruction in transit may be recalled,
returning its permit to the free pool. A book on the shelf may be collected by its patron,
which returns its permit to the free pool.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The permits still free, the permits travelling with instructions in transit,
and the permits under books on the shelf always add up to exactly the shelf's capacity, so the
hold shelf can never be committed beyond what it can hold.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every request that joins the queue eventually leaves it.

---- MODULE W4Od18m6p1t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Nodes, Automations, MaxSetting, MaxLease, NoAck

Copies == [Automations -> 0..MaxSetting]
Acks == [auto : Automations, value : 0..MaxSetting]

VARIABLES record, copy, leaseOf, lease, ack

vars == <<record, copy, leaseOf, lease, ack>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ record \in Copies
    /\ copy \in [Nodes -> Copies]
    /\ leaseOf \in [Nodes -> 0..MaxLease]
    /\ lease \in 0..MaxLease
    /\ ack \in [Nodes -> {NoAck} \cup Acks]

Init ==
    /\ record = [a \in Automations |-> 0]
    /\ copy = [n \in Nodes |-> [a \in Automations |-> 0]]
    /\ leaseOf = [n \in Nodes |-> 0]
    /\ lease = 0
    /\ ack = [n \in Nodes |-> NoAck]

Holder(n) == leaseOf[n] = lease /\ lease > 0

\* Issuing the lease and handing over a fresh copy are the same step, so a
\* working copy can never predate the lease it will be written under.
Issue(n) ==
    /\ lease < MaxLease
    /\ lease' = lease + 1
    /\ leaseOf' = [leaseOf EXCEPT ![n] = lease + 1]
    /\ copy' = [copy EXCEPT ![n] = record]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<record, ack>>

Refresh(n) ==
    /\ Holder(n)
    /\ copy' = [copy EXCEPT ![n] = record]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<record, leaseOf, lease, ack>>

\* A setting is filled in once and never changed, so the record only ever gains
\* settings; a slow node keeps filling in its own copy regardless of the lease.
Adjust(n, a, v) ==
    /\ v > 0
    /\ copy[n][a] = 0
    /\ copy' = [copy EXCEPT ![n] = [copy[n] EXCEPT ![a] = v]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<record, leaseOf, lease, ack>>

\* Only a setting the copy has actually filled in is acknowledged; a blank is
\* not something the record has promised to keep.
WriteBack(n, a) ==
    /\ Holder(n)
    /\ copy[n][a] > 0
    /\ record' = copy[n]
    /\ ack' = [ack EXCEPT ![n] = [auto |-> a, value |-> copy[n][a]]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<copy, leaseOf, lease>>

Reissue ==
    /\ lease = MaxLease
    /\ lease' = 0
    /\ leaseOf' = [n \in Nodes |-> 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<record, copy, ack>>

Next ==
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Issue(n) \/ Refresh(n)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes, a \in Automations, v \in 1..MaxSetting : Adjust(n, a, v)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes, a \in Automations : WriteBack(n, a)
    \/ Reissue

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

AcknowledgedEditsStand ==

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Nodes = {ndHub, ndBridge}
    Automations = {autNight, autAway}
    MaxSetting = 1
    MaxLease = 2
    NoAck = noAck

INVARIANT AcknowledgedEditsStand
nl:
A smart-home door lock network keeps a shared automation record: a setting for each automation
the household runs. A setting starts blank and is filled in exactly once; the record only ever
gains settings and never changes one that is already filled in. Editing is protected by a lease. Only the node holding the lease number
the network most recently issued may write, and a write replaces the whole record with the
editing node's working copy, so a copy that was taken before somebody else's edit landed would
carry that edit away with it.

Issuing a lease hands the new holder a fresh copy of the record in the same breath, and a node
may only refresh its copy while it holds the current lease. That is what keeps a working copy
from ever being older than the lease it is written under. Nodes can be slow but never fail: a
node may go on fiddling with a copy it took under a lease that has since been handed to
somebody else, and it will still be there later, but its writes will no longer be taken.

When a node writes, it is told which automation it has just set and to what, and it holds on to
that acknowledgement.

The network behaves as follows. The next lease number may be issued to any node, so long as the
lease budget is not spent; issuing hands that node a fresh copy of the record. A node holding
the current lease may refresh its copy from the record. Any node may fill in a still-blank automation in
its own working copy, whether or not it holds a lease; it may not change one already filled in. A node holding the current lease may
write its working copy over the record, and is acknowledged for one automation its copy has
actually filled in, together with the value it filled in; a still-blank automation is not
something the record acknowledges. When the lease budget is spent the numbering is reissued from the start and
every node is left holding no lease.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every acknowledgement a node holds still matches the record -- the automation
it names still carries the value it was acknowledged for -- so no acknowledged edit is ever
carried away by a later write reverting it to blank.

---- MODULE W4Od10m9p5t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Crews, Supervisor, Blocks, MaxEpoch, MaxOverrides, NoOne, NoBlock

VARIABLES epoch, roster, assignment, credited, brokenBy, overrides

vars == <<epoch, roster, assignment, credited, brokenBy, overrides>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ epoch \in 1..MaxEpoch
    /\ roster \in SUBSET Crews
    /\ assignment \in [Crews -> {NoBlock} \cup Blocks]
    /\ credited \in [Crews -> {NoBlock} \cup Blocks]
    /\ brokenBy \in [Blocks -> {NoOne} \cup Crews]
    /\ overrides \in 0..MaxOverrides

Init ==
    /\ epoch = 1
    /\ roster = Crews
    /\ assignment = [c \in Crews |-> NoBlock]
    /\ credited = [c \in Crews |-> NoBlock]
    /\ brokenBy = [b \in Blocks |-> NoOne]
    /\ overrides = 0

Assign(c, b) ==
    /\ c \in roster
    /\ assignment[c] = NoBlock
    /\ credited[c] = NoBlock
    /\ brokenBy[b] = NoOne
    /\ assignment' = [assignment EXCEPT ![c] = b]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, roster, credited, brokenBy, overrides>>

\* Breaking the seal is the irreversible step; both records are written with it.
Release(c) ==
    /\ c \in roster
    /\ assignment[c] # NoBlock
    /\ credited[c] = NoBlock
    /\ brokenBy[assignment[c]] = NoOne
    /\ brokenBy' = [brokenBy EXCEPT ![assignment[c]] = c]
    /\ credited' = [credited EXCEPT ![c] = assignment[c]]
    /\ assignment' = [assignment EXCEPT ![c] = NoBlock]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, roster, overrides>>

StandDown(c) ==
    /\ assignment[c] # NoBlock
    /\ assignment' = [assignment EXCEPT ![c] = NoBlock]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, roster, credited, brokenBy, overrides>>

\* The supervisor's override skips the roster and the assignment, but it is still
\* credited, so the block's record and a crew sheet still agree.
Override(b) ==
    /\ overrides < MaxOverrides
    /\ brokenBy[b] = NoOne
    /\ credited[Supervisor] = NoBlock
    /\ brokenBy' = [brokenBy EXCEPT ![b] = Supervisor]
    /\ credited' = [credited EXCEPT ![Supervisor] = b]
    /\ overrides' = overrides + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, roster, assignment>>

\* Reconfiguring under a held assignment would strand a crew mid-release.
Reconfigure(r) ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ r # roster
    /\ \A c \in Crews : assignment[c] = NoBlock
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ roster' = r
    /\ UNCHANGED <<assignment, credited, brokenBy, overrides>>

Renumber ==
    /\ epoch = MaxEpoch
    /\ \A c \in Crews : assignment[c] = NoBlock
    /\ epoch' = 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<roster, assignment, credited, brokenBy, overrides>>

Settle(c) == Release(c) \/ StandDown(c)

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Crews, b \in Blocks : Assign(c, b)
    \/ \E c \in Crews : Settle(c)
    \/ \E b \in Blocks : Override(b)
    \/ \E r \in SUBSET Crews : Reconfigure(r)
    \/ Renumber

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
        /\ \A c \in Crews : WF_vars(Settle(c))

ReleasedAtMostOnce ==
    \A b \in Blocks : brokenBy[b] # NoOne => credited[brokenBy[b]] = b

EveryAssignmentClears ==
    \A c \in Crews : (assignment[c] # NoBlock) ~> (assignment[c] = NoBlock)

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Crews = {crwTrack, crwSignal, crwSuper}
    Supervisor = crwSuper
    Blocks = {blkTunnel, blkViaduct}
    MaxEpoch = 2
    MaxOverrides = 1
    NoOne = noOne
    NoBlock = noBlock

INVARIANT ReleasedAtMostOnce
PROPERTY EveryAssignmentClears
nl:
A subway signalling block system lets maintenance crews release a track block for work. A
release is irreversible: the block's interlock seal is broken for the rest of the session, and
the system records both which crew broke it and, on the crew's own sheet, which block that crew
is credited with. Those two records are what stop a block being released twice -- a second
release would take the block's record away from the first crew while that crew's sheet still
claimed it.

Which crews are on duty is settled by an epoch-numbered reconfiguration. Only a crew on the
current roster may be assigned a block or perform a release, and the roster may only be
reconfigured when no crew is holding an assignment, so a reconfiguration never strands a crew
part-way through a release. The control-room supervisor holds a privileged override and may
break a block's seal directly, without a roster or an assignment, a bounded number of times per
session; the override is still credited on the supervisor's own sheet like any other release.

The system behaves as follows. A crew on the current roster, holding no assignment and not yet
credited with a block, may be assigned a block whose seal is still intact. A crew is credited with at most one release per session. A crew on the roster
that is not yet credited and holds an assignment on a block whose seal is still intact may
release it, which breaks the
seal, records the crew against the block, credits the block on the crew's sheet, and clears the
assignment. A crew holding an assignment may stand down from it instead. The roster may be
reconfigured to any different roster while no crew holds an assignment, which takes the system
to the next epoch. The supervisor may break the seal of a block directly, spending one of the
session's overrides, provided the supervisor is not already credited with a block. When the
epoch numbering is spent and no crew holds an assignment, the numbering restarts.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every block whose seal is broken is credited on the sheet of the very crew
recorded against it, so the irreversible release happens at most once per block.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every assignment a crew takes on is eventually cleared.

---- MODULE W4Od0m6p3t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Teams, Slots, MaxLease, NoGrant

Grants == [slot : Slots, id : 1..MaxLease]
Notices == [to : Teams, slot : Slots, id : 1..MaxLease]

VARIABLES onSlot, holding, issued, circulating

vars == <<onSlot, holding, issued, circulating>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ onSlot \in [Slots -> 0..MaxLease]
    /\ holding \in [Teams -> {NoGrant} \cup Grants]
    /\ issued \in 0..MaxLease
    /\ circulating \in SUBSET Notices

Init ==
    /\ onSlot = [s \in Slots |-> 0]
    /\ holding = [t \in Teams |-> NoGrant]
    /\ issued = 0
    /\ circulating = {}

Grant(t, s) ==
    /\ onSlot[s] = 0
    /\ issued < MaxLease
    /\ issued' = issued + 1
    /\ onSlot' = [onSlot EXCEPT ![s] = issued + 1]
    /\ circulating' = circulating \cup {[to |-> t, slot |-> s, id |-> issued + 1]}
    /\ UNCHANGED holding

\* The number on the slot is the fence: a notice whose number the slot has moved
\* past is a leftover, however plausible it looks.
TakeUp(n) ==
    /\ n \in circulating
    /\ holding[n.to] = NoGrant
    /\ onSlot[n.slot] = n.id
    /\ holding' = [holding EXCEPT ![n.to] = [slot |-> n.slot, id |-> n.id]]
    /\ circulating' = circulating \ {n}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<onSlot, issued>>

Leftover(n) ==
    /\ n \in circulating
    /\ (holding[n.to] # NoGrant \/ onSlot[n.slot] # n.id)
    /\ circulating' = circulating \ {n}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<onSlot, holding, issued>>

GiveUp(t) ==
    /\ holding[t] # NoGrant
    /\ onSlot' = [onSlot EXCEPT ![holding[t].slot] = 0]
    /\ holding' = [holding EXCEPT ![t] = NoGrant]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<issued, circulating>>

\* Pulling a lease takes it off the holder in the same step, so nobody is left
\* holding a number the slot no longer carries.
Pull(s) ==
    /\ onSlot[s] # 0
    /\ onSlot' = [onSlot EXCEPT ![s] = 0]
    /\ holding' = [t \in Teams |->
                     IF holding[t] # NoGrant /\ holding[t].slot = s
                     THEN NoGrant ELSE holding[t]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<issued, circulating>>

Renumber ==
    /\ issued = MaxLease
    /\ \A s \in Slots : onSlot[s] = 0
    /\ \A t \in Teams : holding[t] = NoGrant
    /\ circulating = {}
    /\ issued' = 0
    /\ UNCHANGED <<onSlot, holding, circulating>>

Next ==
    \/ \E t \in Teams, s \in Slots : Grant(t, s)
    \/ \E n \in Notices : TakeUp(n) \/ Leftover(n)
    \/ \E t \in Teams : GiveUp(t)
    \/ \E s \in Slots : Pull(s)
    \/ Renumber

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoSlotHandedTwice ==
    \A t \in Teams :
        holding[t] # NoGrant => onSlot[holding[t].slot] = holding[t].id

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Teams = {tmVascular, tmOrtho}
    Slots = {sltTheatreA, sltTheatreB}
    MaxLease = 3
    NoGrant = noGrant

INVARIANT NoSlotHandedTwice
nl:
A hospital operating-room scheduler hands theatre slots to surgical teams as leases. Every
lease carries a number, and the numbers are handed out in sequence and never reused within a
scheduling round. A slot carries the number of the lease currently on it, or nothing if it is
free, and a team that has taken up a lease holds the slot and the number it was granted.

Grant notices reach the teams out of order and can be arbitrarily late. A team therefore takes
up a notice only if the slot it names still carries exactly the lease number on the notice; a
notice naming a lease number the slot has moved past is a leftover from an earlier grant and is
thrown away. That check is the whole of the defence against a slot being handed to two teams.

Leases expire. When the scheduler pulls a slot's lease it frees the slot and takes the lease
away from whatever team was holding it, so no team is left holding a number the slot no longer
carries.

The scheduler behaves as follows. The scheduler may grant a free slot to a team, taking the
next lease number, marking the slot with it and putting a grant notice into circulation. A
team with no lease in hand may take up a circulating notice addressed to it whose slot still
carries the notice's lease number. A circulating notice addressed to a team that already holds
a lease, or whose slot no longer carries its number, is thrown away. A team holding a lease may
give it up, freeing the slot. The scheduler may pull a slot's lease, freeing the slot and
taking the lease from any team holding it. When the lease numbering is spent and no slot is
leased, no team is holding, and no notice is in circulation, a fresh round of numbering begins.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every team holding a lease finds its slot still carrying exactly the lease
number that team was granted, so a slot is never handed out to a second team while the first
still holds it.

---- MODULE W4Od11m0p5t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Operators, Jobs, Plates, MaxVersion, MinLimit, MaxLimit, NoPlate, NoJob, NoStage

Stagings == [job : Jobs, plate : Plates, base : 0..MaxVersion]

VARIABLES burnedOn, usedBy, version, staged, limit

vars == <<burnedOn, usedBy, version, staged, limit>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ burnedOn \in [Jobs -> {NoPlate} \cup Plates]
    /\ usedBy \in [Plates -> {NoJob} \cup Jobs]
    /\ version \in 0..MaxVersion
    /\ staged \in [Operators -> {NoStage} \cup Stagings]
    /\ limit \in MinLimit..MaxLimit

Init ==
    /\ burnedOn = [j \in Jobs |-> NoPlate]
    /\ usedBy = [p \in Plates |-> NoJob]
    /\ version = 0
    /\ staged = [o \in Operators |-> NoStage]
    /\ limit = MinLimit

InUse == Cardinality({p \in Plates : usedBy[p] # NoJob})

Stage(o, j, p) ==
    /\ staged[o] = NoStage
    /\ burnedOn[j] = NoPlate
    /\ usedBy[p] = NoJob
    /\ staged' = [staged EXCEPT ![o] = [job |-> j, plate |-> p, base |-> version]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<burnedOn, usedBy, version, limit>>

\* The version test is what stops two operators staging against the same board
\* and both burning; the limit test is the shop's current plate ceiling.
Ready(o) ==
    /\ staged[o].base = version
    /\ burnedOn[staged[o].job] = NoPlate
    /\ usedBy[staged[o].plate] = NoJob
    /\ InUse < limit
    /\ version < MaxVersion

Burn(o) ==
    /\ staged[o] # NoStage
    /\ Ready(o)
    /\ burnedOn' = [burnedOn EXCEPT ![staged[o].job] = staged[o].plate]
    /\ usedBy' = [usedBy EXCEPT ![staged[o].plate] = staged[o].job]
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ staged' = [staged EXCEPT ![o] = NoStage]
    /\ UNCHANGED limit

StartOver(o) ==
    /\ staged[o] # NoStage
    /\ ~Ready(o)
    /\ staged' = [staged EXCEPT ![o] = NoStage]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<burnedOn, usedBy, version, limit>>

\* Retuning below what is already in use is allowed; nothing more burns until the
\* count has come back under the limit.
Retune(v) ==
    /\ v # limit
    /\ limit' = v
    /\ UNCHANGED <<burnedOn, usedBy, version, staged>>

Reindex ==
    /\ version = MaxVersion
    /\ version' = 0
    /\ staged' = [o \in Operators |-> NoStage]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<burnedOn, usedBy, limit>>

Settle(o) == Burn(o) \/ StartOver(o)

Next ==
    \/ \E o \in Operators, j \in Jobs, p \in Plates : Stage(o, j, p)
    \/ \E o \in Operators : Settle(o)
    \/ \E v \in MinLimit..MaxLimit : Retune(v)
    \/ Reindex

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
        /\ \A o \in Operators : WF_vars(Settle(o))

BurnedAtMostOnce ==
    \A p \in Plates : usedBy[p] # NoJob => burnedOn[usedBy[p]] = p

EveryStagingClears ==
    \A o \in Operators : (staged[o] # NoStage) ~> (staged[o] = NoStage)

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Operators = {opDay, opNight}
    Jobs = {jobFlyer, jobCarton}
    Plates = {pltCyan, pltBlack}
    MaxVersion = 2
    MinLimit = 1
    MaxLimit = 2
    NoPlate = noPlate
    NoJob = noJob
    NoStage = noStage

INVARIANT BurnedAtMostOnce
PROPERTY EveryStagingClears
nl:
A print shop job spooler burns jobs onto printing plates. Burning is irreversible: the plate is
etched for that job and can never carry another, and the job can never be burned again. The
spooler keeps both halves of that pairing -- the plate a job was burned onto, and the job a
plate was used for -- and a job burned a second time would leave its first plate recorded
against it while the job itself pointed at the second.

Burning goes through optimistic locking. An operator stages the job and plate it intends to
pair, together with the job board's version as it read it. The staging is carried out only if
that version is still the board's version, the job is still unburned, the plate is still
unused, the number of plates in use is below the shop's current plate limit, and the version
numbering has room. Otherwise the staging is thrown away and the operator starts over.

The plate limit is set at runtime and the shop foreman may retune it up or down at any time,
including below the number of plates already in use, in which case nothing more is burned until
the count is back below the limit.

The spooler behaves as follows. An operator with nothing staged may stage an unburned job
against an unused plate, recording the board's version. An operator may carry out its staging
when all of the tests above pass, which burns the job onto the plate, records the pairing both
ways and moves the version on. A staging that fails any test is thrown away and the operator
starts over. The foreman may retune the plate limit to any value in the shop's permitted range.
When the version numbering is spent it is reindexed to the start, which also throws away every
staging.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every plate that has been used is the very plate its job records being burned
onto, so the irreversible burn happens at most once per job.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every staging an operator makes is eventually cleared.

---- MODULE W4Od18m7p0t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Apps, MaxTag, NoOne, NoTag, NoRead

\* A read takes the holder and the tag together; they always move together too,
\* which is what makes the tag a sound test on the pair.
Reads == [who : {NoOne} \cup Apps, tag : 0..MaxTag]

VARIABLES holder, tag, inside, seen

vars == <<holder, tag, inside, seen>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ holder \in {NoOne} \cup Apps
    /\ tag \in 0..MaxTag
    /\ inside \in [Apps -> {NoTag} \cup (0..MaxTag)]
    /\ seen \in [Apps -> {NoRead} \cup Reads]

Init ==
    /\ holder = NoOne
    /\ tag = 0
    /\ inside = [a \in Apps |-> NoTag]
    /\ seen = [a \in Apps |-> NoRead]

Read(a) ==
    /\ seen' = [seen EXCEPT ![a] = [who |-> holder, tag |-> tag]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, tag, inside>>

\* The swap is judged on the tag, not on the picture of the holder the read
\* happened to carry; a slow app's read fails here rather than getting in.
SwapIn(a) ==
    /\ seen[a] # NoRead
    /\ seen[a].tag = tag
    /\ seen[a].who = NoOne
    /\ tag < MaxTag
    /\ holder' = a
    /\ tag' = tag + 1
    /\ inside' = [inside EXCEPT ![a] = tag + 1]
    /\ seen' = [seen EXCEPT ![a] = NoRead]

Leave(a) ==
    /\ inside[a] # NoTag
    /\ tag < MaxTag
    /\ holder' = NoOne
    /\ tag' = tag + 1
    /\ inside' = [inside EXCEPT ![a] = NoTag]
    /\ UNCHANGED seen

Abandon(a) ==
    /\ seen[a] # NoRead
    /\ seen[a].tag # tag
    /\ seen' = [seen EXCEPT ![a] = NoRead]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, tag, inside>>

Reseal ==
    /\ tag = MaxTag
    /\ holder = NoOne
    /\ \A a \in Apps : inside[a] = NoTag
    /\ tag' = 0
    /\ seen' = [a \in Apps |-> NoRead]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, inside>>

Next ==
    \/ \E a \in Apps : Read(a) \/ SwapIn(a) \/ Leave(a) \/ Abandon(a)
    \/ Reseal

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

ModeExclusion ==
    \A a \in Apps : inside[a] # NoTag => (holder = a /\ inside[a] = tag)

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Apps = {appPhone, appPanel}
    MaxTag = 3
    NoOne = noOne
    NoTag = noTag
    NoRead = noRead

INVARIANT ModeExclusion
nl:
A smart-home door lock network has one programming mode on its master keypad that only a single
app session may be inside at a time. The right to be inside is held in a compare-and-swap
register carrying two things read together: who holds the mode, and a tag that moves on every
time the register changes. An app reads the pair, and later swaps itself in only if the tag it
read is still the register's tag and the read showed the mode unheld. Because every change moves
the tag, a read taken before somebody else's change can never pass that test.

Apps can be slow but never fail. An app may sit on a read for arbitrarily long before trying to
swap, which is exactly why the tag rather than the read's own picture of the holder is what the
swap is judged on. An app whose read has gone stale abandons it and reads again.

The network behaves as follows. An app may read the register, recording both the holder it saw
and the tag it saw. An app holding a read that showed the mode unheld, whose tag is still the
register's tag and while the tag numbering has room, may swap itself in: it becomes the holder,
the tag moves on, and the app records the tag it entered under. An app inside the mode may leave
while the tag numbering has room, which clears the holder and moves the tag on. An app holding a
read whose tag is no longer the register's tag abandons that read. When the tag numbering is
spent, the mode is unheld and nobody is inside, the register may be resealed: the tag returns to
zero and every outstanding read is thrown away, so no read survives the reseal to be mistaken
for a current one.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every app inside the programming mode is the register's recorded holder and
entered under the tag the register still carries, so two apps can never be inside it at once.

---- MODULE W4Od17m6p5t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS TerminalA, TerminalB, Carts, Bags, Flights, ShiftLength, Span, NoOne, NotSent

Loaders == TerminalA \cup TerminalB

\* Which terminal a loader belongs to decides whether the shared pool already
\* owes that terminal a cart.
SideOf(l) == IF l \in TerminalA THEN TerminalA ELSE TerminalB

VARIABLES stamp, manifest, leaseOf, deadline, clock

vars == <<stamp, manifest, leaseOf, deadline, clock>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ stamp \in [Bags -> {NotSent} \cup Flights]
    /\ manifest \in [Flights -> SUBSET Bags]
    /\ leaseOf \in [Carts -> {NoOne} \cup Loaders]
    /\ deadline \in [Carts -> 0..ShiftLength]
    /\ clock \in 0..ShiftLength

Init ==
    /\ stamp = [b \in Bags |-> NotSent]
    /\ manifest = [f \in Flights |-> {}]
    /\ leaseOf = [c \in Carts |-> NoOne]
    /\ deadline = [c \in Carts |-> 0]
    /\ clock = 0

GrantLease(l, c) ==
    /\ leaseOf[c] = NoOne
    /\ \A x \in SideOf(l) : \A d \in Carts : leaseOf[d] # x
    /\ clock + Span <= ShiftLength
    /\ leaseOf' = [leaseOf EXCEPT ![c] = l]
    /\ deadline' = [deadline EXCEPT ![c] = clock + Span]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stamp, manifest, clock>>

\* Both halves of the record are written together; the bag can never come back.
Dispatch(l, c, b, f) ==
    /\ leaseOf[c] = l
    /\ deadline[c] > clock
    /\ stamp[b] = NotSent
    /\ stamp' = [stamp EXCEPT ![b] = f]
    /\ manifest' = [manifest EXCEPT ![f] = @ \cup {b}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leaseOf, deadline, clock>>

ReturnCart(c) ==
    /\ leaseOf[c] # NoOne
    /\ leaseOf' = [leaseOf EXCEPT ![c] = NoOne]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stamp, manifest, deadline, clock>>

Reclaim(c) ==
    /\ leaseOf[c] # NoOne
    /\ deadline[c] <= clock
    /\ leaseOf' = [leaseOf EXCEPT ![c] = NoOne]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stamp, manifest, deadline, clock>>

Tick ==
    /\ clock < ShiftLength
    /\ clock' = clock + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stamp, manifest, leaseOf, deadline>>

NewShift ==
    /\ clock = ShiftLength
    /\ \A c \in Carts : leaseOf[c] = NoOne
    /\ clock' = 0
    /\ deadline' = [c \in Carts |-> 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stamp, manifest, leaseOf>>

Reclaiming == \E c \in Carts : Reclaim(c)

Next ==
    \/ \E l \in Loaders, c \in Carts : GrantLease(l, c)
    \/ \E l \in Loaders, c \in Carts, b \in Bags, f \in Flights : Dispatch(l, c, b, f)
    \/ \E c \in Carts : ReturnCart(c)
    \/ Reclaiming
    \/ Tick
    \/ NewShift

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(Tick) /\ WF_vars(Reclaiming)

DispatchedOnce == \A f \in Flights : \A b \in manifest[f] : stamp[b] = f

EveryLeasedCartComesBack ==
    \A c \in Carts : (leaseOf[c] # NoOne) ~> (leaseOf[c] = NoOne)

====
nl:
An airport runs two independent baggage routers, one per terminal, that share a single pool of
loading carts. A cart is taken by holding a lease on it, and a lease carries a deadline on the
shift clock; a terminal may hold at most one cart lease across all of its loaders at a time, so
neither terminal can corner the pool.

Dispatching a bag to a flight is irreversible: the bag goes onto that flight's manifest and its
own record is stamped with the flight, and it can never be dispatched again. The manifest and the
bag's own stamp are the two halves that keep this honest -- a bag dispatched a second time would
be left sitting on the first flight's manifest while its stamp named the second.

The routers behave as follows. A loader may be granted a lease on a free cart, provided no loader
on its terminal already holds one and the lease deadline would fall inside the shift; the deadline
is set a fixed span ahead of the clock. A loader holding a cart lease whose deadline is still
ahead of the clock may dispatch a bag that has never been dispatched to a flight, which stamps the
bag with the flight and puts it on that flight's manifest. A loader holding a cart lease may return
the cart to the pool. The clock may tick. A cart whose lease deadline has been reached may be
reclaimed into the pool. When the shift clock has run out and no cart is leased, a fresh shift
begins with the clock back at the start.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every bag on a flight's manifest is stamped with that very flight, so the
irreversible dispatch happens at most once per bag.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every leased cart is eventually returned to the pool.

---- MODULE W4Od11m7p4t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Spoolers, Slots, PoolSize, MaxTag, NoTag

VARIABLES claimed, tag, seenTag, seenFree

vars == <<claimed, tag, seenTag, seenFree>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ claimed \in [Spoolers -> SUBSET Slots]
    /\ tag \in 0..MaxTag
    /\ seenTag \in [Spoolers -> {NoTag} \cup (0..MaxTag)]
    /\ seenFree \in [Spoolers -> SUBSET Slots]

Init ==
    /\ claimed = [s \in Spoolers |-> {}]
    /\ tag = 0
    /\ seenTag = [s \in Spoolers |-> NoTag]
    /\ seenFree = [s \in Spoolers |-> Slots]

Taken == UNION {claimed[s] : s \in Spoolers}

\* The register serves one read at a time.
Read(s) ==
    /\ \A x \in Spoolers : seenTag[x] = NoTag
    /\ seenTag' = [seenTag EXCEPT ![s] = tag]
    /\ seenFree' = [seenFree EXCEPT ![s] = Slots \ Taken]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<claimed, tag>>

\* The claim is judged against what the read saw; the tag test is what makes that
\* picture trustworthy, since a stale one would show the pool emptier than it is.
Claim(s, x) ==
    /\ seenTag[s] = tag
    /\ x \in seenFree[s]
    /\ Cardinality(Slots \ seenFree[s]) < PoolSize
    /\ tag < MaxTag
    /\ claimed' = [claimed EXCEPT ![s] = @ \cup {x}]
    /\ tag' = tag + 1
    /\ seenTag' = [seenTag EXCEPT ![s] = NoTag]
    /\ UNCHANGED seenFree

Release(s, x) ==
    /\ x \in claimed[s]
    /\ tag < MaxTag
    /\ claimed' = [claimed EXCEPT ![s] = @ \ {x}]
    /\ tag' = tag + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<seenTag, seenFree>>

Abandon(s) ==
    /\ seenTag[s] # NoTag
    /\ (seenTag[s] # tag \/ tag = MaxTag)
    /\ seenTag' = [seenTag EXCEPT ![s] = NoTag]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<claimed, tag, seenFree>>

Reseal ==
    /\ tag = MaxTag
    /\ \A x \in Spoolers : seenTag[x] = NoTag
    /\ tag' = 0
    /\ seenFree' = [x \in Spoolers |-> Slots]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<claimed, seenTag>>

Next ==
    \/ \E s \in Spoolers : Read(s) \/ Abandon(s)
    \/ \E s \in Spoolers, x \in Slots : Claim(s, x) \/ Release(s, x)
    \/ Reseal

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

PoolWithinCapacity == Cardinality(Taken) <= PoolSize

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Spoolers = {splDay, splNight}
    Slots = {sltPressA, sltPressB, sltPressC}
    PoolSize = 2
    MaxTag = 3
    NoTag = noTag

INVARIANT PoolWithinCapacity
nl:
A print shop runs two independent job spoolers that draw press slots from one shared pool. The
pool has a capacity that is smaller than the number of slots on the floor: only so many slots may
be claimed at once across both spoolers together, whatever either of them would like.

The pool is guarded by a compare-and-swap register. A spooler reads the register, taking both the
tag it carries and the set of slots that were free at that moment, and later claims a slot only if
the tag it read is still the register's tag. Every claim and every release moves the tag on, so a
read taken before somebody else's change cannot pass. The claim is judged against what the read
saw, not against the live pool -- that is the point of the tag test, since a stale read would show
the pool emptier than it is. The register serves one read at a time.

The shop behaves as follows. A spooler may read the register when no read is outstanding anywhere,
recording the tag and the free set it saw. A spooler holding a read whose tag is still the
register's tag may claim a slot that its read showed free, provided its read also showed the pool
below capacity and the tag numbering has room; claiming records the slot against that spooler and
moves the tag on. A spooler may release a slot it has claimed, which moves the tag on. A spooler
holding a read whose tag is no longer current abandons it, and so does one holding a read taken
once the tag numbering is spent, since no claim can be made against it. When the tag numbering is spent and no
read is outstanding, the register is resealed and the tag returns to zero.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The slots claimed by the two spoolers together never number more than the pool's
capacity.

---- MODULE W4Od7m3p0t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Cranes, Controllers, MaxTerm, MinLifts, MaxLifts, NoOne

VARIABLES onRecord, inBay, leader, term, liftLimit, lifting

vars == <<onRecord, inBay, leader, term, liftLimit, lifting>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ onRecord \in {NoOne} \cup Cranes
    /\ inBay \in SUBSET Cranes
    /\ leader \in Controllers
    /\ term \in 1..MaxTerm
    /\ liftLimit \in MinLifts..MaxLifts
    /\ lifting \in SUBSET Cranes

Init ==
    /\ onRecord = NoOne
    /\ inBay = {}
    /\ leader \in Controllers
    /\ term = 1
    /\ liftLimit = MinLifts
    /\ lifting = {}

Admit(d, c) ==
    /\ d = leader
    /\ onRecord = NoOne
    /\ c \notin lifting
    /\ onRecord' = c
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inBay, leader, term, liftLimit, lifting>>

GoIn(c) ==
    /\ onRecord = c
    /\ c \notin inBay
    /\ inBay' = inBay \cup {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<onRecord, leader, term, liftLimit, lifting>>

ComeOut(c) ==
    /\ c \in inBay
    /\ inBay' = inBay \ {c}
    /\ onRecord' = NoOne
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, liftLimit, lifting>>

StartLift(c) ==
    /\ c \notin lifting
    /\ c \notin inBay
    /\ c # onRecord
    /\ Cardinality(lifting) < liftLimit
    /\ lifting' = lifting \cup {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<onRecord, inBay, leader, term, liftLimit>>

EndLift(c) ==
    /\ c \in lifting
    /\ lifting' = lifting \ {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<onRecord, inBay, leader, term, liftLimit>>

\* Retuning may drop the limit below what is already lifting; nothing new starts
\* until the count has come back under it.
Retune(v) ==
    /\ v # liftLimit
    /\ liftLimit' = v
    /\ UNCHANGED <<onRecord, inBay, leader, term, lifting>>

\* A handover with a crane on record would leave it inside under a record the new
\* leader never wrote, so handover waits for the bay to be clear.
TakeOver(d) ==
    /\ d # leader
    /\ onRecord = NoOne
    /\ term < MaxTerm
    /\ leader' = d
    /\ term' = term + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<onRecord, inBay, liftLimit, lifting>>

Renumber ==
    /\ term = MaxTerm
    /\ onRecord = NoOne
    /\ term' = 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<onRecord, inBay, leader, liftLimit, lifting>>

Entering == \E c \in Cranes : GoIn(c)
Leaving == \E c \in Cranes : ComeOut(c)

Next ==
    \/ \E d \in Controllers, c \in Cranes : Admit(d, c)
    \/ Entering
    \/ Leaving
    \/ \E c \in Cranes : StartLift(c) \/ EndLift(c)
    \/ \E v \in MinLifts..MaxLifts : Retune(v)
    \/ \E d \in Controllers : TakeOver(d)
    \/ Renumber

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(Entering) /\ WF_vars(Leaving)

BayExclusion == inBay \subseteq {onRecord}

AdmissionsClear == (onRecord # NoOne) ~> (onRecord = NoOne)

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Cranes = {crnGantry, crnMobile}
    Controllers = {ctlQuay, ctlYard}
    MaxTerm = 2
    MinLifts = 1
    MaxLifts = 2
    NoOne = noOne

INVARIANT BayExclusion
PROPERTY AdmissionsClear
nl:
A container-ship crane yard has one spreader-change bay that a single crane may be inside at a
time. Access is handed out by whichever controller is currently leading the yard: the leader
records the crane it has admitted, and a crane may only go in once it is the crane on record.
Leadership passes by failover, and a handover is only allowed while the bay stands empty with
nobody admitted, so a change of controller can never leave a crane inside the bay under a record
the new leader never wrote.

Separately, the yard runs ordinary lifts. How many cranes may be lifting at once is set at
runtime and the yard supervisor may retune it up or down at any moment. A crane cannot be lifting
and be admitted to the bay at the same time.

The yard behaves as follows. The leading controller may admit a crane that is not lifting, when
nobody is on record as admitted. A crane on record may go into the bay. A crane inside the bay may
come out, which clears the record. A crane that is neither lifting nor inside the bay may start a
lift while the number of cranes lifting is below the yard's current limit. A crane that is lifting
may finish. The supervisor may retune the lift limit to any value in the yard's permitted range.
A controller other than the leader may take over while nobody is on record as admitted, so long as
the term numbering has room. When the numbering is spent it restarts.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The cranes inside the bay are never anything more than the single crane the
leading controller has on record, so two cranes are never inside it at once.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Whenever a crane is on record as admitted, the record is eventually cleared.

---- MODULE W4Od15m1p4t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Members, RingSize, Levels, Orders, Depth, MaxGen

\* The token goes to the next seat or the one past it, so a quiet member does not
\* stall the whole book.
Onward(m, k) == ((m + k - 1) % RingSize) + 1

VARIABLES book, gen, seat, dead

vars == <<book, gen, seat, dead>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ book \in [Levels -> SUBSET Orders]
    /\ gen \in 1..MaxGen
    /\ seat \in [Members -> 0..MaxGen]
    /\ dead \in SUBSET Members

Init ==
    /\ book = [l \in Levels |-> {}]
    /\ gen = 1
    /\ seat = [m \in Members |-> IF m = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0]
    /\ dead = {}

Resting == UNION {book[l] : l \in Levels}

Seated(m) == m \notin dead /\ seat[m] = gen

\* Nobody alive is seated on the current generation: the ring is stranded.
Stranded == \A m \in Members : seat[m] = gen => m \in dead

Rest(m, l, o) ==
    /\ Seated(m)
    /\ o \notin Resting
    /\ Cardinality(book[l]) < Depth
    /\ book' = [book EXCEPT ![l] = @ \cup {o}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<gen, seat, dead>>

Pull(m, l, o) ==
    /\ Seated(m)
    /\ o \in book[l]
    /\ book' = [book EXCEPT ![l] = @ \ {o}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<gen, seat, dead>>

Pass(m, k) ==
    /\ Seated(m)
    /\ gen < MaxGen
    /\ gen' = gen + 1
    /\ seat' = [seat EXCEPT ![m] = 0, ![Onward(m, k)] = gen + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<book, dead>>

Regenerate(m) ==
    /\ Stranded
    /\ m \notin dead
    /\ gen < MaxGen
    /\ gen' = gen + 1
    /\ seat' = [seat EXCEPT ![m] = gen + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<book, dead>>

Fail(m) ==
    /\ m \notin dead
    /\ Cardinality(dead) < Cardinality(Members) - 1
    /\ dead' = dead \cup {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<book, gen, seat>>

Recover(m) ==
    /\ m \in dead
    /\ dead' = dead \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<book, gen, seat>>

ReForm(m) ==
    /\ gen = MaxGen
    /\ m \notin dead
    /\ gen' = 1
    /\ seat' = [x \in Members |-> IF x = m THEN 1 ELSE 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<book, dead>>

Next ==
    \/ \E m \in Members, l \in Levels, o \in Orders : Rest(m, l, o) \/ Pull(m, l, o)
    \/ \E m \in Members, k \in 1..2 : Pass(m, k)
    \/ \E m \in Members : Regenerate(m) \/ Fail(m) \/ Recover(m) \/ ReForm(m)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

LevelsWithinDepth == \A l \in Levels : Cardinality(book[l]) <= Depth

====
nl:
A stock exchange opening auction keeps a resting order book split by price level. Each level has a
fixed depth: no level may ever hold more resting orders than that. The right to touch the book
travels the exchange's matching members as a numbered token, and a member may rest or pull an
order only while the token generation it is seated on is the ring's current generation; the token
is passed to the next seat or the one past it, taking the next generation.

A member can fail silently, including while seated on the current generation, which strands the
ring. The survivors cannot tell a failed member from a quiet one, so any surviving member may
regenerate the token when no live member is seated on the current generation, minting the next
generation for itself and abandoning the stranded one. When the generation numbering is spent, a
surviving member may re-form the ring, restarting the numbering with itself seated.

The auction behaves as follows. A live member seated on the current generation may rest an order
that is nowhere in the book onto a level that is below its depth. A live member seated on the
current generation may pull an order off the level holding it. A live member seated on the current
generation may pass the token to the next seat or the one past it, taking the next generation, so
long as the numbering has room. Any surviving member may regenerate the token when no live member
is seated on the current generation. Any member may fail silently, so long as not every member has
failed, and a failed member may come back. When the numbering is spent, a surviving member may
re-form the ring.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No price level ever holds more resting orders than its depth allows.

---- MODULE W4Od2m7p1t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Robots, Aisles, MaxStamp, NoOne, NoClaim, NoRead

Claims == [aisle : Aisles, stamp : 1..MaxStamp]
Reads == [aisle : Aisles, stamp : 0..MaxStamp]

VARIABLES owner, stampOf, mine, seen

vars == <<owner, stampOf, mine, seen>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ owner \in [Aisles -> {NoOne} \cup Robots]
    /\ stampOf \in [Aisles -> 0..MaxStamp]
    /\ mine \in [Robots -> {NoClaim} \cup Claims]
    /\ seen \in [Robots -> {NoRead} \cup Reads]

Init ==
    /\ owner = [a \in Aisles |-> NoOne]
    /\ stampOf = [a \in Aisles |-> 0]
    /\ mine = [r \in Robots |-> NoClaim]
    /\ seen = [r \in Robots |-> NoRead]

Read(r, a) ==
    /\ seen' = [seen EXCEPT ![r] = [aisle |-> a, stamp |-> stampOf[a]]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, stampOf, mine>>

\* An aisle is writable only by its owner, so a robot's own write is the only
\* thing that can ever supersede its own write.
Writable(r) ==
    /\ seen[r] # NoRead
    /\ stampOf[seen[r].aisle] = seen[r].stamp
    /\ owner[seen[r].aisle] \in {NoOne, r}
    /\ stampOf[seen[r].aisle] < MaxStamp

Write(r) ==
    /\ Writable(r)
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![seen[r].aisle] = r]
    /\ stampOf' = [stampOf EXCEPT ![seen[r].aisle] = @ + 1]
    /\ mine' = [mine EXCEPT ![r] =
                  [aisle |-> seen[r].aisle, stamp |-> stampOf[seen[r].aisle] + 1]]
    /\ seen' = [seen EXCEPT ![r] = NoRead]

Abandon(r) ==
    /\ seen[r] # NoRead
    /\ ~Writable(r)
    /\ seen' = [seen EXCEPT ![r] = NoRead]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, stampOf, mine>>

\* Giving up an aisle moves its stamp on, so the robot's memory of it goes too.
GiveUp(r, a) ==
    /\ owner[a] = r
    /\ stampOf[a] < MaxStamp
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![a] = NoOne]
    /\ stampOf' = [stampOf EXCEPT ![a] = @ + 1]
    /\ mine' = [mine EXCEPT ![r] = NoClaim]
    /\ UNCHANGED seen

Reindex ==
    /\ \E a \in Aisles : stampOf[a] = MaxStamp
    /\ owner' = [a \in Aisles |-> NoOne]
    /\ stampOf' = [a \in Aisles |-> 0]
    /\ mine' = [r \in Robots |-> NoClaim]
    /\ seen' = [r \in Robots |-> NoRead]

Settle(r) == Write(r) \/ Abandon(r)

Next ==
    \/ \E r \in Robots, a \in Aisles : Read(r, a) \/ GiveUp(r, a)
    \/ \E r \in Robots : Settle(r)
    \/ Reindex

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
        /\ \A r \in Robots : WF_vars(Settle(r))

WritesAreNotOverwritten ==
    \A r \in Robots : mine[r] # NoClaim => stampOf[mine[r].aisle] = mine[r].stamp

EveryReadResolves ==
    \A r \in Robots : (seen[r] # NoRead) ~> (seen[r] = NoRead)

====

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Robots = {rbtPicker, rbtHauler}
    Aisles = {aisEast, aisWest}
    MaxStamp = 2
    NoOne = noOne
    NoClaim = noClaim
    NoRead = noRead

INVARIANT WritesAreNotOverwritten
PROPERTY EveryReadResolves
nl:
A warehouse robot fleet keeps a shared assignment record: for each aisle, which robot is working
it and a stamp that moves on every time that aisle's entry changes. Robots update the record with
a compare-and-swap: a robot reads one aisle's entry, taking the stamp it saw, and later writes only
if that stamp is still the aisle's stamp. An aisle's entry may only be written by the robot that
already owns it or by anyone when it is unowned, so a robot's own write is the only thing that can
supersede its own write.

Robots can be slow but never fail. A robot may sit on a read for arbitrarily long before trying to
write, which is exactly why the stamp rather than the robot's memory of the entry is what the write
is judged on. A read that can no longer be written is abandoned and the robot reads again.

When a robot writes, it remembers the aisle and the stamp its write produced, and that memory is
what it relies on afterwards.

The fleet behaves as follows. A robot may read any aisle's entry, recording the aisle and the stamp
it saw. A robot holding a read may write when the aisle's stamp is still the one it read, the aisle
is either unowned or already its own, and the stamp numbering has room; writing takes ownership,
moves the aisle's stamp on and records the aisle and new stamp as the robot's own. A robot holding a
read it cannot write abandons it. A robot may give up an aisle it owns, which leaves the aisle
unowned, moves its stamp on and clears that robot's memory of it. When the stamp numbering is spent
the record is reindexed: every stamp returns to zero, every aisle is left unowned, and every
memory and outstanding read is cleared.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every robot that remembers writing an aisle finds that aisle still carrying
exactly the stamp its write produced, so no robot's write is ever silently overwritten.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every read a robot takes is eventually resolved, leaving it holding no read.

---- MODULE W4Od13m0p1t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Machines, MaxCoins, MaxVersion, MaxAdd, MinHopper, MaxHopper, NoStage

Stagings == [add : 1..MaxAdd, base : 0..MaxVersion]

VARIABLES float, version, accounted, staged, hopper

vars == <<float, version, accounted, staged, hopper>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ float \in [Machines -> 0..MaxCoins]
    /\ version \in 0..MaxVersion
    /\ accounted \in SUBSET (0..MaxVersion)
    /\ staged \in [Machines -> {NoStage} \cup Stagings]
    /\ hopper \in MinHopper..MaxHopper

Init ==
    /\ float = [m \in Machines |-> 0]
    /\ version = 0
    /\ accounted = {}
    /\ staged = [m \in Machines |-> NoStage]
    /\ hopper = MinHopper

Stage(m, d) ==
    /\ staged[m] = NoStage
    /\ staged' = [staged EXCEPT ![m] = [add |-> d, base |-> version]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<float, version, accounted, hopper>>

\* The base test is what stops a change worked out against an older record from
\* consuming a version step that another change already took.
Applicable(m) ==
    /\ staged[m].base = version
    /\ float[m] + staged[m].add <= hopper
    /\ version < MaxVersion

Apply(m) ==
    /\ staged[m] # NoStage
    /\ Applicable(m)
    /\ float' = [float EXCEPT ![m] = @ + staged[m].add]
    /\ accounted' = accounted \cup {version}
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ staged' = [staged EXCEPT ![m] = NoStage]
    /\ UNCHANGED hopper

StartOver(m) ==
    /\ staged[m] # NoStage
    /\ ~Applicable(m)
    /\ staged' = [staged EXCEPT ![m] = NoStage]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<float, version, accounted, hopper>>

\* Retuning below what a machine already holds is allowed; it simply takes
\* nothing more until it has been emptied down.
Retune(v) ==
    /\ v # hopper
    /\ hopper' = v
    /\ UNCHANGED <<float, version, accounted, staged>>

Collect(m) ==
    /\ float[m] > 0
    /\ float' = [float EXCEPT ![m] = @ - 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, accounted, staged, hopper>>

Next ==
    \/ \E m \in Machines, d \in 1..MaxAdd : Stage(m, d)
    \/ \E m \in Machines : Apply(m) \/ StartOver(m) \/ Collect(m)
    \/ \E v \in MinHopper..MaxHopper : Retune(v)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

EveryVersionStepAccounted == accounted = 0..(version - 1)

====

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Machines = {vmAtrium, vmGarage}
    MaxCoins = 2
    MaxVersion = 2
    MaxAdd = 1
    MinHopper = 1
    MaxHopper = 2
    NoStage = noStage

INVARIANT EveryVersionStepAccounted
nl:
A vending machine network keeps a shared coin-float record holding a coin count for each machine,
together with a version that moves on by one every time a float change is applied. Changes go
through optimistic locking: a machine stages the number of coins it wants to add together with the
version it read, and the staged change is applied only if that version is still the record's
version. The network also keeps, for audit, the set of version steps that have actually been
accounted for by an applied change.

Hopper capacity is set at runtime and the route operator may retune it up or down at any moment,
including below what a machine is already holding, in which case that machine simply takes nothing
more until it has been emptied down.

The network behaves as follows. A machine with nothing staged may stage a number of coins to add,
recording the record's version as it stands. A machine may apply its staged change when the version
it staged against is still the record's version, the machine's count plus the coins would stay
within the current hopper capacity, and the version numbering has room; applying raises that
machine's count, records the version step it consumed in the audit set, and moves the version on. A
staged change failing any of those tests is thrown away and the machine starts over. The operator
may retune the hopper capacity to any value in the network's permitted range. A machine's coins may
be collected one at a time, which does not touch the version.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The audit set of accounted-for version steps is exactly the gapless run from zero
up to one below the record's current version, so every version step the record has taken was
consumed by exactly one applied change and none was overwritten unseen.

---- MODULE W4Od9m0p1t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Desks, MaxLog, MaxShed, MaxStep, NoPrep

Preps == [base : 0..MaxLog, mw : 1..MaxStep]

VARIABLES dispatch, toldIndex, prepared, shedTotal

vars == <<dispatch, toldIndex, prepared, shedTotal>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ dispatch \in Seq(Desks)
    /\ Len(dispatch) <= MaxLog
    /\ toldIndex \in [Desks -> 0..MaxLog]
    /\ prepared \in [Desks -> {NoPrep} \cup Preps]
    /\ shedTotal \in [Desks -> 0..MaxShed]

Init ==
    /\ dispatch = << >>
    /\ toldIndex = [d \in Desks |-> 0]
    /\ prepared = [d \in Desks |-> NoPrep]
    /\ shedTotal = [d \in Desks |-> 0]

Prepare(d, w) ==
    /\ prepared[d] = NoPrep
    /\ prepared' = [prepared EXCEPT ![d] = [base |-> Len(dispatch), mw |-> w]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<dispatch, toldIndex, shedTotal>>

\* The length the desk read is the lock: if the log has grown, somebody else's
\* entry is already at the index this one was aiming for.
Lands(d) ==
    /\ prepared[d].base = Len(dispatch)
    /\ Len(dispatch) < MaxLog
    /\ shedTotal[d] + prepared[d].mw <= MaxShed

Append1(d) ==
    /\ prepared[d] # NoPrep
    /\ Lands(d)
    /\ dispatch' = Append(dispatch, d)
    /\ toldIndex' = [toldIndex EXCEPT ![d] = Len(dispatch) + 1]
    /\ shedTotal' = [shedTotal EXCEPT ![d] = @ + prepared[d].mw]
    /\ prepared' = [prepared EXCEPT ![d] = NoPrep]

StartAgain(d) ==
    /\ prepared[d] # NoPrep
    /\ ~Lands(d)
    /\ prepared' = [prepared EXCEPT ![d] = NoPrep]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<dispatch, toldIndex, shedTotal>>

Restore(d) ==
    /\ shedTotal[d] > 0
    /\ shedTotal' = [shedTotal EXCEPT ![d] = @ - 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<dispatch, toldIndex, prepared>>

\* Rolling the log makes every index a desk was told meaningless, so they go too.
Roll ==
    /\ Len(dispatch) = MaxLog
    /\ \A d \in Desks : prepared[d] = NoPrep
    /\ dispatch' = << >>
    /\ toldIndex' = [d \in Desks |-> 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<prepared, shedTotal>>

Settle(d) == Append1(d) \/ StartAgain(d)

Next ==
    \/ \E d \in Desks, w \in 1..MaxStep : Prepare(d, w)
    \/ \E d \in Desks : Settle(d) \/ Restore(d)
    \/ Roll

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
        /\ \A d \in Desks : WF_vars(Settle(d))

Standing(d) == toldIndex[d] <= Len(dispatch) /\ dispatch[toldIndex[d]] = d

NoLandedAppendLost == \A d \in Desks : toldIndex[d] # 0 => Standing(d)

EveryPreparationClears ==
    \A d \in Desks : (prepared[d] # NoPrep) ~> (prepared[d] = NoPrep)

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Desks = {dskCoastal, dskInland}
    MaxLog = 2
    MaxShed = 2
    MaxStep = 1
    NoPrep = noPrep

INVARIANT NoLandedAppendLost
PROPERTY EveryPreparationClears
nl:
A power-grid load shedder writes every shed instruction into a shared append-only dispatch log.
Control desks append under optimistic locking: a desk prepares an instruction together with the log
length it read, and the append lands only if the log is still that length. If another desk got
there first the log has grown, the prepared instruction is thrown away, and the desk starts again.
When an append lands, the desk is told the index its entry occupies, and that index is what it
relies on from then on.

Desks can be slow but never fail. A prepared instruction may sit for arbitrarily long before the
desk tries to append it, which is exactly why the length the desk read, rather than the desk's own
sense of where the log stood, is what the append is judged on.

Each desk also carries a running total of megawatts it has shed, capped by its allowance; shed load
may be restored one megawatt at a time. When the log has run to its full length and no desk has an
instruction prepared, the log is rolled: it is emptied and every index a desk was told is cleared,
since those indices mean nothing against a fresh log.

The shedder behaves as follows. A desk with nothing prepared may prepare an instruction for a number
of megawatts, recording the log's current length. A desk may append its prepared instruction when
the log is still that length, the log has room, and its running total would stay within its
allowance; appending adds its entry to the end of the log, tells the desk the index it landed at,
and raises its running total. A prepared instruction failing any of those tests is thrown away and
the desk starts again. A desk may restore a megawatt of shed load. When the log is full and nothing
is prepared anywhere, the log may be rolled.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever a desk has been told an index for its entry, the log still runs at least
that far and that index still holds that desk's entry, so no landed append is ever overwritten or
lost.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every instruction a desk prepares is eventually cleared.
